title: Human Anatomy Quick Revision
shortDescription: A one-page, 10-second review of every system and organ covered in this subject — the final pass before an exam.
genZNote: The whole subject, compressed into one last scroll before you close the app.

questions.prompt: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta and out to the body.

questions.prompt: Which structure carries urine from the bladder OUT of the body?
questions.explanation: The urethra carries urine out of the body; ureters carry urine from kidney to bladder.
optionNotes: Kidney to bladder, not bladder to outside.

questions.explanation: The thyroid gland secretes calcitonin (lowers blood calcium), alongside T3/T4. The parathyroid glands secrete PTH (raises blood calcium).

questions.prompt: Which connective structure attaches muscle to bone?
questions.explanation: A tendon connects muscle to bone; a ligament connects bone to bone.

questions.prompt: Which nervous-system division includes only the brain and spinal cord?
questions.explanation: The CNS is made up of the brain and spinal cord; everything else (all nerves) is the PNS.
Insulin lowers blood glucose. Glucagon, cortisol, and adrenaline all tend to raise it.
optionNotes: Tends to raise blood glucose during stress.
Tends to raise blood glucose during fight-or-flight.

sections.heading: Body Systems — 10-Second Review
bullets: Cardiovascular — heart pumps blood in one loop: body → RA → RV → lungs → LA → LV → body.
Respiratory — nose → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli (gas exchange).
Digestive — mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum → anus, plus liver/gallbladder/pancreas.
Nervous — CNS (brain + spinal cord) processes; PNS carries signals to/from it.
Skeletal — axial (skull, spine, ribs) + appendicular (limbs); support, protection, movement, minerals, blood cells.
Urinary — kidney filters blood via nephrons → ureter → bladder → urethra.
Endocrine — hypothalamus → pituitary → target glands, all via hormones and negative feedback.
Lymphatic/Immune — lymph nodes filter lymph; spleen filters blood; innate (fast) vs. adaptive (specific, has memory) immunity.
Reproductive — male: testis → epididymis → vas deferens → urethra. Female: ovary → fallopian tube → uterus → cervix → vagina.
Integumentary — epidermis (outer) → dermis (glands, follicles, nerves) → hypodermis (fat).

sections.heading: Organs and Senses — 10-Second Review
bullets: Eye — cornea → pupil (iris) → lens → retina → optic nerve → brain.
Ear — pinna → ear canal → eardrum → ossicles → cochlea (hearing) / semicircular canals (balance).
Nose — odor molecules → nasal cavity receptors → olfactory nerves → olfactory bulb → brain.
Tongue — fungiform, foliate, circumvallate papillae have taste buds; filiform papillae give texture only.
Liver — produces bile, processes nutrients, detoxifies blood (gallbladder only stores bile).
Kidney — nephron is the filtering unit; filtration → reabsorption → secretion → urine.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: A single consolidated summary of every Human Anatomy chapter's most important, most-tested fact.
keyFacts: Eleven body systems: cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, nervous, skeletal, muscular, urinary, endocrine, lymphatic/immune, reproductive, integumentary.
Four senses covered individually: eye, ear, nose, tongue — plus skin as a sensory organ within the integumentary system.
The five most commonly confused term-pairs across the whole subject: ureter/urethra, insulin/glucagon, PTH/calcitonin, tendon/ligament, pulmonary artery/vein.
commonConfusion: Treat this page as a final check, not a first read — each fact here is explained in full in its own chapter.

highYieldFacts: Pulmonary vessels are the one exception to "arteries = oxygenated, veins = deoxygenated".
PTH and calcitonin have opposite effects on blood calcium; insulin and glucagon have opposite effects on blood glucose.
Ureter (kidney → bladder) vs. urethra (bladder → outside) is one of the most frequently tested spelling-and-function pairs.
commonTraps: Don't rely on this page alone for a first-time read of any topic — it deliberately omits explanation in favor of the bare fact.
mustRemember: Revisit the individual chapter for any bullet here that doesn't immediately make sense — this page assumes the full lesson has already been read once.
